newsitem.title: USA: S. Calif. home values continue to decline - report.
newsitem.headline: S. Calif. home values continue to decline - report.

text.p: Home values in northern California may be stable, but in the state's southern counties homeowners continue to lose equity by about five percent a year, according to a report released on Monday.

Real estate information service Experian said in the report that home values in the San Francisco Bay area counties of Santa Clara, Sonoma, San Mateo and San Francisco have remained almost unchanged from last year.
By contrast, in southern California, San Bernardino County recorded the largest decline of 6.2 percent, followed by Los Angeles and Riverside counties.
Experian said, however, that the rate of decline in southern California home values has slowed from previous years, raising the prospect of a more stable market in 1997.

"A 20 percent surge in housing demand in California that we have witnessed so far this year has helped firm up home values," said Nima Nattagh, Experian's market analyst. "But demand has not elevated to a point where homeowners can expect solid equity gains in the near future."
Experian's figures track the resale value of the same homes.
